summary: Nirbhay N. Singh works in Buddhist studies. He served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor of Psychiatry, Pediatrics, and Psychology at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a historian and Tibetologist. Educated at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, he was founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at the University of Calcutta (1971).
Nirupam Chakma specializes in Buddhist studies. Chakma earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Gal completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Wolfson College, Oxford, earning a D.Phil. in 2003 under Richard Gombrich, and learned under Shlomo Biderman. She has served as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He taught at the University of Tokyo (Professor Emeritus 1981–1994) and Taisho University (~1994–2008), and presided over several international academic associations.

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he served as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1973–1999) and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei and Kanagawa Universities.
Noboru Ueda (b. 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Otani and Kyoto Universities under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, and others, he served as Professor at Otani University (~1980–2010) and president of Otani Junior College (~2006–2010).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara, Kobayashi held assistant professor posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979), and taught at Taisho University (attested 2026).

Nobuhiro Ota (b. 1969) is an Indology and history scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. After a fellowship at Tokyo, he joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming associate professor in 2007 and professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University. He held a post as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (b. 1932) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1955–1959) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1968–1975).

Tensho Miyazaki (b. 1978) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2005–2011) and held research posts at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo.

Nobumi Iyanaga (b. 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at EPHE. He held a research contract with EFEO (2008–2014) and served as a lecturer at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003).
Nobuo Otsuka (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (b. 1960) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein and also studied under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji (b. 1936) is a Sinologist and philosopher. Educated at Kyoto and Tohoku Universities, he served as a professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and institute director at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase (b. 1941) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

Nobuyuki Yamagiwa (b. 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
